Title: TOM: Question - Vial of Garou Blood

Messages.Author: Shane Travis
Messages.Body:
Text on the vial is as follows:

Vial of Garou Glood Equipment 1 pool
If a vampire is equipped with this Vial, you may burn this card before
range is chosen in a round of combat. This vampire then gets +1 hand
damage and an additional strike each round for the remainder of combat;
he or she cannot use other equipment cards during that combat.

Since this card gives an additional strike, does it preclude a minion
playing any other cards to gain further additional strikes? IIRC, the
ruling is that only one card may be played to gain additional strikes.

Part of me says yes; this is an emotional argument, however, as it is just
too obscene to think of a Blur'd, Vial'd vampire doing 8 points in a
single round...

Part of me says no; The Vial was not 'played' per se, but merely brought
into use. If there was a vampire which had as its special ability "This
vampire may pay 1 blood for one additional strike each round" then I
would not think that this special ability would prevent this vampire from
playing additional strike cards, would it?

>Part of me says yes; this is an emotional argument, however, as it is just
>too obscene to think of a Blur'd, Vial'd vampire doing 8 points in a
>single round...
>
>Part of me says no; The Vial was not 'played' per se, but merely brought
>into use. If there was a vampire which had as its special ability "This
>vampire may pay 1 blood for one additional strike each round" then I
>would not think that this special ability would prevent this vampire from
>playing additional strike cards, would it?

Messy, messy, messy. If one extends the ruling that you can play Trap
and then press to end, then using the vial doesn't really count as having
played an additional strike card... at least, not in later round.
It does seems like you had played one in that round, so couldn't play
another, which is bizarre. I'm also not sure whether or not your
hypothetical vampire should or shouldn't be able to use its ability
and still use Blur.

Long answer: this will require some discussion back at the home office.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:

Jyhad rulebook:
Only one card may give an additional strike to a minion for each round of
combat.

VTES Rulebook:
Only one additional strike card may be used by a minion for each round of
combat.

It seems in this case, the Jyhad wording would clear up the mess in
a logical fashion. The vial of Garou blood would be the "card" that
gave the minion an additional strike, therefore precluding any other
card being used on *any* round that the vial was in effect.

It wouldn't be too hard to read the VtES rulebook this way, but it is easy
enough to read it the other way as well.

Similarly for the hypothetical vampire: The vampire's own card is the one
that gave it an additional strike, therefore no other card would be
allowed to. The VtES rules are much harder to make this happenstance
behave "properly".

Messages.Body:
Mage Bob <Denni...@crpl.cedar-rapids.lib.ia.us> writes:

>sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L. Scott Johnson) wrote:
>>VTES Rulebook:
>>Only one additional strike card may be used by a minion for each round >of combat.

>this is obvious...

>The VIAL gives the VAMP an aditional strike USABLE EVERY ROUND OF THE
>COMBAT.... hence you can blur a vialed vamp because you can only play
>one card "for each round of combat" or perhaps if you wanna get really
>techie... you could use a Blur the second round of a combat with your
>vailed vamp, but not the first as the add strike card fer that round was
>in fact the vial... see... easy...

Notes:
1. used != played
2. the vial is a card which gives a vampire additional strikes

Not so obvious, to me.

The vial is a card which has been used by a minion (vampire) for an extra
strike *every round*.

And, since "only one additional strike card may be used by a minion for
each round", then no more may be played.

This is simply an ambiguity of the rules, which, as my original post was
attempting to demonstrate, was avoided by the Jyhad rules (although the
Jyhad rules could be interpretted as allowing more than one additional
strike card to be sluffed with no effect).
